newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Deputy PM says Gazprom CEO out of line.
newsitem.headline: Deputy PM says Gazprom CEO out of line.

text.p: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alfred Kokh said on Thursday that the head of Russian natural gas monopoly Gazprom was out of line for criticising the government.
He told a news conference that the government should examine what he called Rem Vyakhirev's personal control of a 35 percent state stake in the company.
Vyakhirev, speaking before the Duma lower house of parliament on Wednesday, said foreign oil and gas companies were working through the government against Gazprom.

"When the chief executive of a company, having administrative control over a government packet of shares, criticises his beneficiary for some action, that is nonsense in my view and should be liquidated soon," Kokh said.
He said the government could annul the agreement or change the terms under which Gazprom manages the stake.
Russia renewed Vyakhirev's control of the 35 percent stake, originally granted in 1993, last year, Kokh said.
Kokh, Russia's privatisation minister, was recently promoted in a new cabinet which intends to reform natural monopolies such as Gazprom.

Gazprom is the world's largest natural gas company. It has in the past been the target of negative comments about its revenues, secrecy and tax-free stabilisation fund, now liquidated, but has usually managed to deflect the criticism.
